newsitem.title: USA: USDA proposses hike in grain inspection fees.
newsitem.headline: USDA proposses hike in grain inspection fees.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Tuesday it wants to increase fees for inspection and weighing services performed by the Federal Grain Inspection Service for U.S. grain exporters.

In a proposed rule published in the Federal Register, the agency said the proposed 3 percent increase in fees would raise an estimated $218,100 for a total of $22.2 million in revenue projected for fiscal 1997. The additional money raised by the increase would be used to pay cost-of-living salary increases for inspectors.
USDA said it would accept comments on the proposal until May 28.
Most U.S. grain exports must be inspected and weighted at 37 export facilities.
USDA said it was also considering other fee increases, including an adjustment to the per metric ton administrative fee to recover the indirect costs of field offices.
